intro: Hiller sits near Brownsville in Fayette County, in a part of the county built up around coal mining and river commerce along the Monongahela. Families here frequently hold mineral interests that trace back to early-20th-century severances, inherited across multiple generations without much documentation changing hands along the way.
We buy mineral and royalty interests near Hiller, including small fractional shares and interests where the current owner isn't entirely sure what document controls their rights.

sections.heading: Brownsville-area mineral history
paragraphs: This part of Fayette County has a long coal and river-commerce history that shaped how mineral rights were originally divided, often separately from surface ownership. We start any review by tracing that history through the recorded deeds.

sections.heading: What to expect from us
paragraphs: We review your documents, pull county records as needed, and give you a straightforward explanation of what we can offer and why, with no pressure to accept.

We'll tell you honestly if a small fractional share's value is modest, rather than overstating what it's likely worth. We'll also explain how Brownsville-area river commerce history occasionally shows up in older recorded easements, even though it rarely changes who actually holds the oil and gas rights themselves.

faqs.question: I'm not sure what document controls my mineral rights near Hiller. Can you help figure that out?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's a normal part of our process — we pull and review the recorded chain of title through the Fayette County Recorder of Deeds to confirm what you actually own before discussing value.

faqs.question: Is there drilling activity near Hiller?
faqs.answer: Activity in this part of Fayette County is present but not dense, so it depends heavily on the specific tract's proximity to current units.

faqs.question: Can you buy a small fractional interest inherited near Hiller?
faqs.answer: Yes, small fractional interests from multi-generation family land are common in this area and we regularly purchase them.

faqs.question: What's the difference between a fractional interest and a full mineral interest near Hiller?
faqs.answer: A full interest means you own all the oil and gas rights under a tract; a fractional interest means you own a percentage, often because it was divided among heirs. We buy either, valued according to the percentage owned.
